newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Nearly fifty hurt in clashes in Bangladesh.
newsitem.headline: Nearly fifty hurt in clashes in Bangladesh.

text.p: Nearly fifty people were injured on Saturday in clashes between tribespeople and Bengali-speaking settlers in Bangladesh's southeastern Chittagong Hill Tracts, police said.
Violence erupted after tribespeople assaulted a Bengali for alleged pick-pocketing at a market in Khagrachhari hill district.
Bengalis, angered by the incident, attacked tribal villagers in what later turned into a savage battle between the two groups, police said.
At least 13 of the injured -- both Bengalis and tribespeople -- were in critical condition, police said on Saturday night.

The 5,500 square-mile (14,200 sq-km) Hill Tracts, bordering India and Burma, have been a scene of tribal insurgency since 1973, in which over 8,500 people have been killed, according to official figures.
The tribespeople, known as the Shanti Bahini, want the Hill Tracts be granted political autonomy and made their exclusive homeland, something Bangladesh has rejected.
